synergies.spec1: Enable Hot-Reload for MCP Clients in Development Mode
synergies.description: Hot-reload enables rapid testing of MCP vessel code changes, which is essential for developing and maintaining MCP-only architecture. Developers can modify metabob-cli vessel code and test changes immediately without restarting opencode.
synergies.benefit: Reduced development iteration time. Faster debugging. Better development experience for MCP-only architecture.
synergies.implementation: Use 'opencode mcp reload' after restarting metabob-cli vessel to pick up code changes

reasons: No shared files with contradictory changes
All changes are additive (new functions, new commands)
Error handling is graceful (errors logged, not thrown)

potentialIssues.mitigation: reload() is idempotent. Can be called multiple times safely. Errors collected and returned.
canReloadSafely() exists but not fully implemented. Currently always returns true. Manual reload gives user control.
potentialIssues.futureWork: Implement full safety checks: detect active MCP tool calls, running activities, open sub-sessions

futureEnhancements: Implement full canReloadSafely() checks to detect active operations
Add automatic reload on vessel restart detection
Create generic MCP health check for all clients (not just Metabob)
Consider reload throttling if multiple config changes occur rapidly
testing: Run manual integration test with metabob-cli vessel
Verify reload works with multiple MCP clients configured
Test reload under load (active sessions, running activities)
Monitor logs for connection close/reopen messages

thisSpec.entry: User runs 'opencode mcp reload' OR config file changes
thisSpec.transform: MCP.reload() closes old clients, re-reads config, re-initializes clients
thisSpec.validate: Returns success status and errors per client
thisSpec.exit: New MCP clients active, old connections closed

patterns: Graceful error handling (collect errors, don't throw)
Integration via existing config reload system
architecturalCompliance.notes: Implementation follows all established architectural patterns. Clean integration with existing systems.
